CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow up of chronic medical problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Anna is a 44-year-old female with a past medical history significant for arthritis, gout, and reflux presenting for follow-up of her chronic problems. Last visit was approximately six months ago.

Arthritis: Patient reports her arthritis is improving. She has been doing pilates and lifting weights to build muscle and reduce joint pain. She completed physical therapy for her right knee with good results and has regained her strength. She is now able to walk 1 to 1.5 miles per day.

Gout: Patient had an episode approximately two months ago affecting her right first big toe. The episode improved with medication. She is currently taking allopurinol without issues and reports no further flare-ups.

Reflux: Patient was started on omeprazole and advised to make dietary modifications. She has started making some dietary modifications but has not completely eliminated certain foods. She continues to have episodes with morning vomiting and also reports abdominal pain and bloating. Last bowel movement was two days ago and was normal without blood. She denies weight loss, fever, and chills.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and abdominal distension. Patient denies diarrhea, weight loss, fever, and chills.

Arthritis
Gout
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Omeprazole 40 milligrams once daily
Allopurinol 100 milligrams once daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs are stable and reassuring.
Heart: Sounds normal.
Lungs: Sound clear.
Abdomen: Tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant without rebound, guarding, or peritoneal signs.
Right knee: Effusion present with mild pain on palpation and decreased range of motion.

RESULTS
Autoimmune panel: Within normal limits.
Right knee x-ray: No fracture. Residual arthritis present.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Reflux, nausea, and vomiting: Right upper quadrant ultrasound ordered to rule out gallstones. Laboratory studies to be obtained. Continue omeprazole 40 milligrams once daily. Continue dietary modifications.

2. Gout: Currently well-controlled on allopurinol. Continue allopurinol 100 milligrams once daily. Refill ordered.

3. Arthritis: Right knee improving with physical therapy and exercise. Continue pilates and continued use of knee. Will reassess with further imaging or intervention if needed.
